deities: Goddess Chamunda (as Chhoti Mata, the younger mother)
festivals: Ashvin (Shardiya) Navratri — 9-day mela on Tekri; lakhs of pilgrims

history.dynasty: Revered by the Puar rulers of Dewas Senior/Junior states (Chamunda is their Kuldevi); the present shrine was constructed by Tara Raje, sister of the Gwalior ruler Madhavrao Scindia and wife of Krishnajirao Puar II of Dewas Senior
history.period: Disputed — sources claim 9th century or 1100–1200 years old; local belief holds the site ancient ('anaadi kaal')
history.summary: The Chamunda Devi shrine on Dewas Tekri — a ~300-ft conical hill above the city — is the 'Chhoti Mata' (younger mother) temple of the hill's two sister goddesses. The image of the goddess is cut into the wall of a cave called Devi Vashini ('the goddess's residence'), from which the city's name Dewas (dev-vas) is said to derive. Local legend describes Dewas Tekri as a Rakt Peeth where drops of Mata Sati's blood fell, and the self-manifested idols of Chamunda and Tulja Bhavani appeared here. For centuries the goddess was known as 'Rakt (bloody) Chamunda' due to the animal-sacrifice (bali) tradition, which ended after the government ban. King Bharthari (brother of Vikramaditya) is traditionally said to have done penance here. E. M. Forster wrote about the shrine in 'The Hill of Devi' (1953). Swami Shivom Tirtha recorded the hill's history in 'Sadhan Shikhar'. The temple shares the Tekri hilltop with the Tulja Bhavani (Badi Mata) shrine — the elder sister — and Bhairav Baba's shrine; parikrama begins at Tulja Bhavani and concludes at Chamunda.

name: Maa Chamunda Devi Temple
town_description: Dewas is a historic industrial city in western Madhya Pradesh, about 35 km northeast of Indore on the Malwa plateau. Its identity is dominated by the Tekri, a 300-ft hill in the middle of the city crowned by the two sister-goddess temples, and it was the seat of two princely states (Dewas Senior and Junior) under the Puars and Marathas. Devotees also pass through Dewas on Indore–Ujjain–Omkareshwar pilgrimage circuits.
